LESSON: GUIDED WRITING GRAMMAR HANDWRITING PUNCTUATION SENTENCE STRUCTURE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Writing 3. 5 Guided writing Handwriting Punctuation Vocabulary Grammar Clarity B
Topic 3.6: Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why is proper sequencing of information important while writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write common words with correct orthography
2. write common words with correct orthography
3. spell in writing common words with correct orthography
4. construct simple sentences using correct structures

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Guided Writing Grammar Handwriting Punctuation Sentence structure makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Play matching games on grooming jointly,
2. Fill gaps in simple dialogues using simple vocabulary of weather patterns, (il fait beau à ... /mauvais, il pleut, il y a du vent, il fait nuageux...) Why is correct orthography important? 54
3. Fill gaps in simple dialogues using simple vocabulary of locating, (à côté de, derrière, en face de, entre) and areas in school (bibliothèque, cantine, infirmerie, salle de classe)
4. Filling in missing letters.
5. Peer education; practice with peers.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is proper sequencing of information important while writing?
2. How can you improve your handwriting?
3. Why is correct orthography important?
4. What makes your handwriting unique?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
